prompt: Find the derivative for  the function: f(x)=(3x-1)/(x^2-2x-3).
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 correctly applies the quotient rule and simplifies to the correct derivative (-3x^2 + 2x - 11)/(x^2 - 2x - 3)^2. Candidates 2 and 4 follow the same method but make an arithmetic error in the numerator’s constant term, yielding -7 instead of -11. Candidate 3 has a similar arithmetic/simplification mistake but also gets the x-term wrong (producing -3x^2 - 2x - 7 instead of -3x^2 + 2x - 11).
